title: sse: fix streaming chunking and framing for partial JSON & delimiter edge cases
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: production customers reported intermittent malformed events from the SSE streaming endpoint when the server emitted partial JSON objects across multiple token frames. Symptoms included extra delimiters ("\n\n"), truncated JSON objects when chunk boundaries coincided with unicode/codepoint splits, and out-of-order 'event:' lines in the OpenAI-compat streaming adapter. This caused downstream SDKs to fail JSON.parse on streamed 'delta' payloads and made function/tool-calling brittle.

This PR fixes the chunking and framing logic across the native SSE streamer and the OpenAI compatibility layer: 1) rework the framing state machine so partial JSON tokens are buffered at the byte level (not codepoint level) and only emitted when a full UTF-8 sequence is available; 2) remove an extra delimiter insertion that occurred when the last token of a flush was an empty string; 3) ensure 'event:' header ordering and newline semantics match the OpenAI streaming contract so consumers receive event/frame pairs predictably; 4) add deterministic unit + integration tests and a regression harness that replays the exact tokenization that previously failed.

This is a behavioral fix with no public API change. It impacts both the runtime (service/sse) and the openai-compat adapter used by many SDKs. The PR includes focused tests, a stress test that reproduces the original bug, and an e2e test against the TS SDK to verify parsing stability. Related Linear tickets: ENG-1423 (streaming stability), ENG-1499 (openai-compat regressions).
commits: Fix: buffer partial UTF-8 bytes in sse streamer to avoid codepoint splits
Fix: canonicalize delimiter insertion path to avoid double-newline when last token empty
Fix: enforce event: then data: ordering in openai_compat streaming adapter
Test: add unit tests for chunk boundary cases and unicode splitting
Test: add integration e2e that replays production token traces
Chore: add comments and docstring for framing state machine
files_changed: service/sse/streamer.py - rework framing state machine and buffer logic
api/openai_compat/streaming_adapter.go - enforce header ordering and canonical delimiters
sdk/ts/src/streaming/parser.ts - add more robust event assembly for edge cases
tests/unit/test_sse_chunking.py - new tests for partial JSON and unicode boundaries
docs/streaming.md - document guaranteed ordering and delimiter semantics
ci/flake_runners.yaml - add longer timeout for streaming integration job
review_comments: Evan Morris (reviewer): Please add a test that simulates a 1-byte-at-a-time network yield for a multi-byte emoji. Previous failures repro with that pattern. Response: Added test_sse_chunking.py::test_multi_byte_emoji_chunking which simulates 1-byte yields and asserts proper reconstruction.

Lina Chen (reviewer): The openai_compat adapter previously relied on strings; switching to byte buffers may affect existing code paths - did you run the ts/sdk e2e? Response: Yes, added an e2e against sdk/ts that validates the SDK parser receives valid 'data: ' payloads and JSON.parse succeeds for function-calling payloads.

Marco Ruiz (approver): Verified with local stress run (10k events) and the replay fixture — LGTM after small nits. Nits addressed: tightened error messages and added a defensive assert around zero-length writes.
Aisha Patel (author): Note that we maintain backward compatibility with consumers: framing still emits the same logical event/data lines; only emission timing and internal buffering changed.
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (all new and existing green)
integration-streaming: pass (replay harness and ts-sdk e2e)
release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming framing and chunking - prevents partial-JSON tokenization across frames, removes extra delimiters, and aligns OpenAI-compat event ordering. Improves stability for streaming function/tool-calling and structured output parsing.
notes: This addresses a customer incident filed via support (SUP-987). QA and SDK owners have been notified; recommend patch release to the hosted API and a follow-up rollout plan for Dedicated nodes to pick up the runtime binary.
